paragraphs.text: 1. I GRASP at you when power and strength begin to dawn: bedew ye, Indra and the Maruts, Heaven and Earth,
paragraphs.original: आ व ऋञ्जस ऊर्जां व्युष्टिष्विन्द्रं मरुतो रोदसी अनक्तन ।
paragraphs.translit: ā va ṛñjasa ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣvindraṃ maruto rodasī anaktana |

paragraphs.text: That Day and Night, in every hall of sacrifice, may wait on us and bless us when they first spring forth.
paragraphs.original: उभे यथा नो अहनी सचाभुवा सदःसदो वरिवस्यात उद्भिदा
paragraphs.translit: ubhe yathā no ahanī sacābhuvā sadaḥsado varivasyāta udbhidā

paragraphs.text: 2. Press the libation out, most excellent of all: the Pressing-stone is grasped like a hand-guided steed.
paragraphs.original: तदु श्रेष्ठं सवनं सुनोतनात्यो न हस्तयतो अद्रिः सोतरि ।
paragraphs.translit: tadu śreṣṭhaṃ savanaṃ sunotanātyo na hastayato adriḥ sotari |

paragraphs.text: So let it win the valour that subdues the foe, and the fleet courser's might that speeds to ample wealth.
paragraphs.original: विदद्ध्यर्यो अभिभूति पौंस्यं महो राये चित्तरुते यदर्वतः
paragraphs.translit: vidaddhyaryo abhibhūti pauṃsyaṃ maho rāye cittarute yadarvataḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. Juice that this Stone pours out removes defect of ours, as in old time it brought prosperity to man.
paragraphs.original: तदिद्ध्यस्य सवनं विवेरपो यथा पुरा मनवे गातुमश्रेत् ।
paragraphs.translit: tadiddhyasya savanaṃ viverapo yathā purā manave gātumaśret |

paragraphs.text: At sacrifices they established holy rites on Tvastar's milk-blent juice bright with the hue of steeds.
4. Drive ye the treacherous demons far away from us: keep Nirrti afar and banish Penury.
paragraphs.original: अप हत रक्षसो भङ्गुरावत स्कभायत निरृतिं सेधतामतिम् ।
paragraphs.translit: apa hata rakṣaso bhaṅgurāvata skabhāyata nirṛtiṃ sedhatāmatim |

paragraphs.text: Pour riches forth for us with troops of hero sons, and bear ye up, O Stones, the song that visits Gods.
paragraphs.original: आ नो रयिं सर्ववीरं सुनोतन देवाव्यं भरत श्लोकमद्रयः
paragraphs.translit: ā no rayiṃ sarvavīraṃ sunotana devāvyaṃ bharata ślokamadrayaḥ

paragraphs.text: 5. To you who are more mighty than the heavens themselves, who, finishing your task with more than Vibhvan's speed,
More rapidly than Vayu seize the Soma juice, better than Agni give us food, to you I sing.
6. Stirred be the glorious Stones: let it press out the juice, the Stone with heavenly song that reaches up to heaven,
paragraphs.original: भुरन्तु नो यशसः सोत्वन्धसो ग्रावाणो वाचा दिविता दिवित्मता ।
paragraphs.translit: bhurantu no yaśasaḥ sotvandhaso grāvāṇo vācā divitā divitmatā |

paragraphs.text: There where the men draw forth the meath for which they long, sending their voice around in rivalry of speed.
paragraphs.original: नरो यत्र दुहते काम्यं मध्वाघोषयन्तो अभितो मिथस्तुरः
paragraphs.translit: naro yatra duhate kāmyaṃ madhvāghoṣayanto abhito mithasturaḥ

paragraphs.text: 7. The Stones press out the Soma, swift as car-borne men, and, eager for the spoil, drain forth the sap thereof
paragraphs.original: सुन्वन्ति सोमं रथिरासो अद्रयो निरस्य रसं गविषो दुहन्ति ते ।
paragraphs.translit: sunvanti somaṃ rathirāso adrayo nirasya rasaṃ gaviṣo duhanti te |

paragraphs.text: To fill the beaker, they exhaust the udder's store, as the men purify oblations with their lips.
paragraphs.original: दुहन्त्यूधरुपसेचनाय कं नरो हव्या न मर्जयन्त आसभिः
paragraphs.translit: duhantyūdharupasecanāya kaṃ naro havyā na marjayanta āsabhiḥ

paragraphs.text: 8. Ye, present men, have been most skillful in your work, even ye, O Stones who pressed Soma for Indra's drink.
paragraphs.original: एते नरः स्वपसो अभूतन य इन्द्राय सुनुथ सोममद्रयः ।
paragraphs.translit: ete naraḥ svapaso abhūtana ya indrāya sunutha somamadrayaḥ |

paragraphs.text: May all ye have of fair go to the Heavenly Race, and all your treasure to the earthly worshipper.
paragraphs.original: वामंवामं वो दिव्याय धाम्ने वसुवसु वः पार्थिवाय सुन्वते
paragraphs.translit: vāmaṃvāmaṃ vo divyāya dhāmne vasuvasu vaḥ pārthivāya sunvate
